name: animal-imagemasking

frames.best_why: Both animal silhouettes are fully formed and centred with no cursor or overlay.

tagline: Landscapes masked into a cat head and a panda head.
summary: Two side-by-side photos each masked into an animal silhouette: a warm sunset scene shaped like a cat with pointed ears, and a misty forest shaped like a round-eared panda.
appearance: On a black stage, two square photos are cut to animal silhouettes. Left is a cat head with two sharp ears above a round face, filled by a peach sunset with a dark treeline. Right is a panda head, a round face with two circular ears, filled by misty green forest.
demo_content: Sunset landscape in a cat mask; misty forest in a panda mask.
search_phrases: picture masked into an animal head
use_when: A playful section or kids' brand wants photos cut into recognisable animal silhouettes.
avoid_when: The masks are loaded from local SVG files, so the effect breaks unless those assets are shipped.
customise: Both image URLs and their mask file names are hardcoded; swapping photos or animals means editing the two figures and supplying new SVG masks in public.
weight_why: Two CSS-masked images with no animation or script.

a11y.note: Both photos have empty alt text, so the landscapes and animal shapes are entirely unavailable to screen readers.

issues: Both images have empty alt text.
The effect depends on /cat.svg and /panda.svg existing in public; without them the images show as plain squares.
polish_why: Clean masking and pleasant photos; no motion and empty alt text make it a one-trick effect.
